newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Lower House panel delays vote on oil bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Lower House panel delays vote on oil bill.

text.p: A lower house committee vote on a bill regulating the opening up of Brazil's oil industry will not be held until next week, officials said.

This morning's session was suspended after government-allied parties failed to agree on a possible amendment to the bill which would allow for the future privatization of Petrobras, according to deputy Alberto Goldman, the head of the lower house committee.
Officials said it was unlikely that a vote in the committee would take place before late Tuesday, March 11.
However, the committee will meet later today at 1900 local time/1700 EST to discuss the bill.

The oil bill would allow private companies to compete or go into partnership with Petrobras. It would also create a new regulator to oversee the oil and gas sector and end fuel price subsidies within three years.
